invention.ref_zh: 小亚细亚吕底亚王国铸造带有狮首官印的琥珀金硬币（约公元前640—前600年）

mass_production.ref: Ancient China independently casts standardized hollow-handle bronze spade money (kongshoubu) in the Central Plains
mass_production.ref_zh: 中国中原地区独立铸造空首布等青铜铲币，确立青铜金属铸币传统

popularization.ref: Qin Dynasty standardizes Chinese currency with circular Ban Liang coins featuring a square hole
popularization.ref_zh: 秦始皇统一中国并颁行秦半两，确立圆形方孔钱规制，深刻影响东亚两千年

sources.title: A History of the World in 100 Objects: Early Lydian Coin — British Museum

notes: 作为国家信用与标准重量保证的金属铸币起源于多中心演化：公元前七至六世纪，小亚细亚吕底亚首创官印冲压琥珀金币，奠定西方打制金银币传统；同期中国中原由贝币演化出空首布等浇铸青铜币，开创东方方孔钱体系。两者工艺与源流独立，具体起源时序与首创权在学界历来并称并存。
notes_en: Standardized metal coinage originated independently in multiple ancient centers: in the 7th–6th century BCE, Lydia in Asia Minor created stamped electrum coins that founded the Western struck-coin tradition, while the Central Plains of China developed cast-bronze spade money, founding the East Asian tradition. Their independent chronologies and distinct metallurgy form a widely acknowledged historical divergence.
summary_zh: 约公元前七至六世纪，吕底亚王国首创官印打制琥珀金币，中国中原独立铸造青铜布币；硬币为贸易确立了标准化国家信用与交换尺度。
summary_en: Emerging in the 7th–6th century BCE via Lydian stamped electrum in Anatolia and bronze spade money in ancient China, coins established standardized state-certified currency for human trade.
